payload.title: The observability dashboard's validation failed_count counts every validation_runs row with a non-ok status, so each red-first proof's deliberate red run at the base commit is recorded as a failed validation run
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/observability.py:99-110 (failed_count counts every non-ok row of the ledger)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/observability.py:66 (the dashboard reads the whole validation_runs ledger)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:503-510 (each proof runs the pin at the base and at the tip through _run_one, one ledger row each)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:797-800 (a red base run is the expected outcome of a proof)
payload.rule_violated: A measurement counts what it names (observability.py:82-88, E21-a: readers must not miscount the unified validation surface); a run whose failure is the evidence is not a failed validation.
payload.notes: Every finding-origin delivery with a proof, and every D6 seat-pin proof, appends a red row at red_at to validation/validation-runs.jsonl on purpose. The nightly dashboard row then reports failed_count and status_counts that include those rows, so a cycle with only successful proofs shows validation failures. No decision reads that block today (reflection renders rolling_slo and alerts), so the wrong number is recorded, not acted on. Close condition: Exclude proof and bench runs (their change_id and validation_plan_id family, or an explicit run purpose field) from _validation_summary, or report them under a separate key; a test where a proven red-first pair leaves failed_count unchanged. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
